title: Distributed representations of behaviour-derived object dimensions in the human visual system
goal: Reproduce the original Figure2 full-66D encoding result and separately exceed its strongest relevant author comparator on exactly the same original input information, participants, response rows, folds and source metric; retain complete map/companion coverage and report both information conditions separately.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: complete original Figure2 encoding map family and required source permutation/noise-ceiling companions under primary-endpoint-v1/reproduction.v2.json.
Improvement: same original endpoint against the strongest relevant author comparator under primary-endpoint-v1/improvement.v1.json; no complete-panel superiority criterion is fabricated.
Separate paper_data and paper_data_author_code evidence for both outcomes; biological attribution/shape reproduction remains separately preserved.
success_criteria: Assess original-endpoint reproduction and improvement independently; a source-faithful computation and independently verified complete outputs are required.
Preserve all3participants, original repeated rows, complete eligible voxel masks and12source folds, with source metric and full companion coverage.
Require strongest relevant source-author calibration, meaningful complete-support comparison and justified dependence-aware uncertainty before a scientific improvement claim.
Follow primary-endpoint-v1/access-conditions.v1.json without exposing evaluator labels or author answers. All protocol and result outcomes remain unresolved/unknown.

Treat new holdouts, input additions, altered populations and convenient scalar substitutions as extensions. A Figure2 gain does not establish Figure6 attribution or whole-paper biological improvement.

lineage_and_loader_evidence.input_scope: Selected Figure2 task uses original complete three-participant single-trial response tables, voxel/stimulus/session metadata and image-wise66D features. Noise-ceiling maps and source permutation companions remain required source outputs; category/shape inputs remain attached only to the separately preserved broader biological scope.
